title: How to Remove Rootkit Windows 10? - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Rootkits are malevolent software programs designed to give programmers with unauthorized privileges to your computer system. They operate stealthily, permitting attackers to spy on your activities, take individual data, and even install extra malware without your information. Given their stealthy nature, rootkits can be particularly challenging to identify and remove. In this article, we’ll go over a few successful strategies to distinguish and evacuate rootkits from your Windows 10 computer.

    • Method 2: Use a Rootkit Removal Tool
    • Method 3: Run Windows Defender Offline

    • Method 5: Restore Windows to a Previous State

What is a Rootkit?

A rootkit is a sort of malware that inserts itself deep inside your system, allowing programmers privileged access. These programs frequently stay hidden, making conventional antivirus software insufficient for detection and removal. Rootkits may come bundled with genuine software or downloaded incidentally from untrustworthy sources. The primary risk with rootkits is their ability to compromise delicate information, bypass security conventions, and install additional malware.

Signs of a Rootkit Infection

Rootkits can be troublesome to identify, but there are a few signs that may recommend your system is compromised:

  • System performance degradation: If your computer is slower than normal or hangs regularly, a rootkit might be using system resources in the background.
  • Strange network activity: Unexpected spikes in network traffic might indicate data being sent to outside servers.
  • Unauthorized access: Sudden password changes or unexpected access to records and folders may imply at a rootkit.
  • Disabled antivirus and firewall: A few rootkits are programmed to disable your security computer program, clearing out your system vulnerable.

If you notice any of these side effects, it’s time to examine further. Below, we talk about strategies to remove rootkits from your Windows 10 computer.

Method 1: Boot into Safe Mode

Booting your computer in Safe Mode limits the operating system to basic capacities, possibly anticipating the rootkit from loading. Here’s how:

Step 1: Restart your computer and hold down the Shift key while clicking Restart.

Step 2:Once your computer reboots, select Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings.

Step 3: Press F4 or 4 to boot into Safe Mode.

Step 4: In Safe Mode, run a full system scan with your antivirus software to distinguish any covered up threats.

Method 2: Use a Rootkit Removal Tool

Rootkits require specialized tools for discovering and removal. There are different trustworthy anti-rootkit instruments available, such as:

  • Malwarebytes Anti-Rootkit: A dedicated tool for rootkit discovery, Malwarebytes Anti-Rootkit is known for its powerful scanning capabilities.
  • Kaspersky TDSSKiller: This tool specializes in identifying and evacuating the TDSS family of rootkits and is effective against other common rootkits as well.
  • Bitdefender Rootkit Remover: Bitdefender’s tool is successful against several well-known rootkits and works nearby your main antivirus software.

To use these tools: Download a rootkit remover from a trusted source.

  • Install and run the tool following the on-screen instructions.
  • Allow the tool to perform a full scan and remove any identified threats.

Method 3: Run Windows Defender Offline

Windows Defender Offline is a effective tool built into Windows 10 that helps identify and remove diligent threats, counting rootkits. To run it:

Step 1:Open Settings > Update & Security > Windows Security.

Step 2:Click on Virus & Threat Protection > Scan options.

Step 3: Select Microsoft Shield Offline scan and click Scan now.

Step 4: Your computer will restart, and Windows Defender Offline will start filtering for rootkits and other threats.

After the scan, any distinguished dangers will be removed, and your system will restart.

Method 4: Use System File Checker (SFC) and DISM Commands

Sometimes, rootkits can corrupt basic system files, which makes it troublesome for regular antivirus program to work accurately. In such cases, utilizing built-in Windows tools like System File Checker (SFC) and Deployment Imaging Service and Management Tool (DISM) can offer assistance repair corrupted files.

  • Open Command Prompt as an administrator (type cmd in the Start menu, right-click, and select Run as administrator).
    • Type sfc /scannow and press Enter. SFC will filter and attempt to repair any undermined files.
    • Once the SFC scan is complete, run the DISM command for advance repair. Type:
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth

This command will look for and repair any issues inside your Windows 10 installation.

After completing these steps, restart your computer and re-run your antivirus software to check if the rootkit has been removed.

Method 5: Restore Windows to a Previous State

If the rootkit contamination is recent, restoring your computer to a past state can help remove it. In any case, this strategy only works if you had enabled System Restore previously.

  • Type System Restore in the Windows search bar and select Create a restore point.
  • Click on System Restore and select a restore point from a date some time recently you noticed any rootkit symptoms.
  • Follow the on-screen informational to restore your system.

Tips to Anticipate Future Rootkit Infections

Preventing rootkits from entering your system is essential for long-term security. Here are a few tips to keep your computer safe:

  1. Keep software up-to-date: Routinely update Windows, drivers, and applications to secure against vulnerabilities.
  2. Use trustworthy antivirus software: Introduce and maintain a reliable antivirus program with dynamic rootkit protection.
  3. Avoid untrusted downloads: Download program only from official or confirmed sources.
  4. Regularly back up information: This will offer assistance you recoup basic records if malware strikes.

Conclusion

Rootkits are modern dangers that require a centered approach for expulsion. By using specialized tools, employing Windows Defender Offline, and following best practices for avoidance, you can keep your Windows 10 system secure. With a proactive approach to security, you can dodge rootkit infections and protect your personal information.
